S.S. Empress of Asia
Chinese Sea
Feb. 12,1933.
Dear Eat hort
We have left the harbor of Nagasaki and are bound for Shanghai where we are
due at 3P.li, tomorrow. The Chinege orew are all be ans to be getting baok althou
most all of them d- this Corona - it jumps a few spaces after the letter
and the letter "t" so that just as I get going full spead ahead that always happens)
come from Canton, which is still several days farther on.
They are awfully funny.
I can understand them better than the average green horn passenger because of all
the training I have had from Hebe. They have some of he r
failings, but the one
letter which none
of them can pronounce is "r". Groeger delights in making them
try, and just lately, one of the old timers on the ship who has lived in the Orient
most of his life, gave Groeger a whole list to try out on the poor Chinese stewards
and dining room
boys. We occasionally have
fried rice on the menu. He always orders
it and then gets one of the boys to tell him what it is. The answer is more humor-
ous than it is appetising -
"flied lice". There are two Englishmen on board who are
great friends and have adjoiming staterooms. One
of them is quite fat. The other
morning the slender one called the room stewa rd assigned to them and told him that
he wanted his bath. The
steward replied "Master
can no have bath". After some talk
on the
subject which became rather heated on the part of the Englishman, the
steward said-
"Master can no have bath - Fat Master kettchie bath now". Meaning of
course that the other Englishman had the only available tub in use.
I have done a little
shop looking but have been terribly disappointed
for the shops are not at all like they used to be when I was here before . The Japs
have gone in for the cheapest kind of olap trap late ly
influenced no doubt by
what the Amer
ican trade wants. None of the old workmanship which characterized
all Japanese things, and none
of the artistic things. Instead just a lot of cheap
poorly constructed
gaudy gadgets which you can see at any Japanese auction in the
United States or at any Woolworth
store.
Their boxes are glued toge the r
and
the reptoductions of Fuji are
in red or bright green. Of course everything is very
cheap
as the "Yen" which is normally worth fifty cents is now worth only 22.
It
makes anyone who knew the
Japan of years ago, however, very sad to realize
that t he things we liked are gone completely and will never come
back.
Their
buildings in the cities too show signs of the worst in European and American arch-
itecture.
One new building in Tokyo which is under construction now is copied
after those new trick buildings which you see ocaasionally in Rotorgravuee sect-
ions,
built in Germany. Of course they think of all the new things as denoting
progress
and I guess that is right but wish they might have developed
some adapt-
ation of their own architecture which would harmonize with the demands of modern
business and yet retain the atmosphere of old Japan. I am hoping that
the small
towns
away from the large centens may still retain some of their Japanese aspect.
We stay in Shanghai until Tuesday morning at ten thirty. I am going to
be ver y
busy for I have
a number of peopiu to see, cables to decipher and ot hers
to put
into code and ge t off. It is pretty nice however to be able to get back on
the
ship and just
take life easy once
the rush is over.
We have
been out of
touch with newspapers do long that I feel that almost anything may have happenad.
Now of course we shall get English papers from Hong Kong, and may be able to find
out what has haken place at least in the "Empiah" as most of our English friends
on board call England. My address will continue to be National City Bank of N.Y.
Shanghai. Mail will be forwarded from thereto where ever I may happen to be. The
weather is better now but st ill cold. They say it will probably be colde r in
Shanghai, warm in Hong Kong and very hot in Manila - which as you know is right
down my alley.

time. There wee be little time
ter me houri do all banko, etc.
to go through cuatomo Eva of yon
ashok with out bags. Lot of red taps
I hair radiord Nate Cit, to sand
any cables to boat.
Hops you
